newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss extend Mobutu's visa on medical grounds.
newsitem.headline: Swiss extend Mobutu's visa on medical grounds.

text.p: The Swiss foreign ministry on Thursday extended a visa for Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko on medical grounds, a ministry spokesman said.

Spokesman Hans-Ruedi Bortis told Reuters that Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti had personally made the decision. But he declined to say how long the visa for Mobutu, operated on for prostate cancer in Lausanne on August 22, would be valid.
"Minister Cotti has extended the visa for Mr. Mobutu on medical grounds," said spokesman Bortis, speaking from the Swiss capital of Berne.
"Each time it is extended it is for a fixed period. But I cannot say for how long," he added.

Swiss media say Mobutu has been receiving chemotheraphy as an outpatient at Lausanne Univeristy Hospital, where he underwent surgery. Swiss television reported he would need to continue the treatment until December.

The extension gives Mobutu his third visa since he arrived in Switzerland in mid-August and comes amid growing criticism from parliamentarians and media about the presence of a man widely regarded as leading an increasingly corrupt and brutal regime.
In Kinshasa on Wednesday, a spokesman for the 66-year-old president denied that he required chemotherapy and said he was convalescing normally.
On Wednesday night, French-language Swiss Television showed brief film footage, which it said was taken last Friday, of Mobutu leaving his luxury hotel in Lausanne and getting into a waiting car.
He was accompanied by his wife and an aide, both holding him by the arm as he walked down the stairs to the car.
Several Swiss parliamentarians have criticised Swiss authorities for admitting Mobutu, including a prominent politician from Vaud canton (state), where Lausanne is located.
Parliamentarian Jozef Zisyadis told Swiss television on Wednesday: "It is outrageous that this dictator be on the Vaud territory. I urge that his visa not be extended."
A visiting correspondent on Tuesday found Zairean bodyguards roaming the corridors of the Beau Rivage hotel, where Mobutu and his entourage of more than 20 are staying.
She was told Mobutu was holidaying in the nearby Alpine resort of Interlaken. Hospital officials refused to discuss his health.
